We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 3 reactions, using templates 1914393, 1914394, 1914395 in this order.

We have applied template 1914393 to target molecule, got precursors: ('COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1').

So first reaction splits target into two fragments: fragment A = COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1 (call it fragment A) and fragment B = FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1 (fragment B). Good.

Now we need to apply template 1914394 to each fragment? The order says use templates in this order, likely sequentially: first 1914393, then 1914394, then 1914395. Probably each reaction applies to one of the fragments from previous step. We need at least 3 reactions total, so we can apply 1914394 to fragment B (since we tried on fragment A and got no result). Indeed applying 1914394 to fragment B gave precursors: ('ClCCl', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1'). So second reaction splits fragment B into ClCCl (dichloromethane?) and FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1 (a simpler amine). Good.

Now we need third reaction using template 1914395. Likely apply to the fragment from second reaction that still contains F? The template 1914395 appears to convert a fluorinated heterocycle to an oxygen analog (maybe dehalogenation). The retro_smarts: '[F;D1;H0:5]-[CH;D3;+0:1]1-[C:2]-[#7:3]-[C:4]-1>>O-[CH;D3;+0:1]1-[C:2]-[#7:3]-[C:4]-1' So it replaces a fluorine attached to a carbon in a 5-membered ring with OH. So the forward reaction is fluorination; retro is defluorination to OH. So to apply retro, we need a molecule with that fluorine pattern. Our fragment B after first step is FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. That contains a fluorine attached to carbon in a ring (maybe matches). The second reaction gave FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1 (no Cl). That still has F attached to carbon in a ring. So we can apply template 1914395 to that fragment to replace F with OH, giving O... maybe OCH? Let's apply.
